body.statement: If \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), then \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{or}}(P,\pi)=G_0\) for every \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_I\). Strict ascent prevents revisiting an order, and Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) makes every terminal order topological; Condition 19 configurations and causal minimality then make residual-independence pruning delete exactly the nonedges. The search uses at most \(d!-1\) insertions and \(d(d-1)d!\) gain comparisons. Memoization uses at most \(d2^{d-1}\) conditional-risk queries and \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC queries, followed by at most \(d(d-1)/2\) pruning checks.
body.justification: The primitive certificate is useful only if it yields a complete labelled-DAG recovery theorem and a finite oracle budget.
body.gap: Solus, Wang, and Uhler (2021, Proposition 8 and Theorem 9) study covered-arrow walks for sparsity, while Li et al. (2025) do not give primitive risk and dependence query counts for GENE.
body.consumer: An implementation can cache the finite local-score table and know its worst-case population-query budget.
